ASX ANNOUNCEMENT
ASX: 1AI |16 October 2026
Algorae Pharmaceuticals Partners with Peter MacCallum Cancer Centre for
Third AI-driven Drug Synergy Screening Program
Highlights
• Algorae Pharmaceuticals has entered into an agreement with the Victorian Centre for
Functional Genomics (VCFG) at Peter MacCallum Cancer Centre for a third program
to independently validate predictions generated by the AlgoraeOS v2 (AOS2) multi-
anchor program.
• Forty high-priority drug combination candidates will be screened for synergy across
four cancer cell lines representing glioblastoma, non-small cell lung cancer, colorectal
cancer and bladder cancer.
• Candidate combinations were selected for validation from the multi-anchor program
(announced 18 May 2026) which evaluated 18 anchor drugs in combination with
thousands of approved and investigational compounds.
• This program is supported by a Therapeutic Innovation Australia Pipeline Accelerator
voucher of $49,109 awarded to the Company to support experimental work in
partnership with the VCFG.
• The project is expected to be completed within six months.
AI-enabled pharmaceutical company Algorae Pharmaceuticals Ltd (ASX: 1AI) has entered
into an agreement with the Victorian Centre for Functional Genomics (“VCFG”) at Peter
MacCallum Cancer Centre (“Peter Mac”) for a third program to independently validate the
predictions from the AOS2 multi-anchor program.
As announced on 18 May 2026, Algorae completed a preliminary examination of the AOS2
prediction set which evaluated 18 anchor drugs in combination with thousands of approved
and investigational compounds across a panel of human cell lines, representing over 9 million
potential drug–drug–cell line combinations. The 18 anchors were selected to span a diverse
range of therapeutic areas and mechanisms of action. Following analysis of commercial and
intellectual property considerations, 40 high-priority drug combination candidates have been
selected for preclinical validation. The combinations selected use a subset of the anchors
chosen for the in silico analysis.
Under the agreement, VCFG will perform compound synergy interaction screens using its high-
throughput technologies and synergy assessment methodologies. The collaboration is
designed to evaluate the predicted synergy of drug combinations across four distinct cancer
cell lines: glioblastoma, non-small cell lung cancer, colorectal cancer and bladder cancer.

Commenting on the collaboration, Algorae Chief Scientific Officer, Dr James McKenna said:
“This study builds on the foundations established through our previous two collaborations with
the VCFG team at the Peter MacCallum Cancer Centre. It represents another important step
in the development of AOS2, allowing us to assess the real-world generalisability of the platform
across multiple anchor drugs. Importantly, the study also provides a further demonstration of
how AOS can help bridge the gap between in silico prediction and biological validation.”
AOS2 multi-anchor program
The multi-anchor prediction set evaluated 18 anchor drugs in combination with thousands of
approved and investigational compounds across a panel of human cell lines. Each prediction
in the dataset included the four well-recognised synergy metrics (ZIP, Bliss, HSA and Loewe)
alongside confidence-weighted measures of predictive uncertainty. Prioritisation thresholds
were informed by, and refined from, the methodology successfully applied to the previous
AOS2 prediction set. These thresholds balance the magnitude of predicted synergy with
uncertainty reduction and biological generalisability across multiple cell lines.
In summary:
AOS2 evaluated over 9 million potential drug–drug–cell line combinations across the 18
anchor drugs. From this prediction set, initial filtering identified:
• more than 478,000 individual synergy predictions passing preliminary synergy and
uncertainty thresholds;
• over 6,000 drug combinations demonstrating predicted synergy across multiple cell
lines, indicating greater biological robustness.
To further prioritise candidates for empirical validation, anchor-specific considerations and
additional filters were then applied, reflecting the predicted strength of synergy, biological
generalisability, and commercial and intellectual property relevance.
This program is supported by a competitive voucher of $49,109 awarded to the Company
under the Phenomics Australia – Therapeutic Innovation Australia Pipeline Accelerator 2025-26
Round 2 scheme, to support experimental work in partnership with the VCFG.
The scheme attracted 28 applications, of which 13 were selected for funding, and the award
reduces the total cost to the Company of accessing these services.
Empirical validation and timeline
The program will investigate 40 drug combinations selected from the multi-anchor prediction
set. Only a subset of the 18 investigated anchors has been progressed.
The screening process, to be performed by VCFG at Peter Mac using its high-throughput
microscopy platform, will include:
• Cell growth optimisation for the high-throughput platform.
• Single-agent dose-response curves across four cancer cell lines.
• Synergy screens using selected dose ranges.

Data analysis will be completed within three weeks of the synergy screen, with the full dataset
expected within six months. Key decision points will be integrated into the study to ensure data
quality and optimise further testing.
Implications and next steps
This work builds on the independent preclinical validation of AlgoraeOS v1 (AOS1) at Peter
Mac (refer ASX announcement dated 5 December 2025) and AOS2 (refer ASX announcement
dated 3 July 2026).
Promising candidates identified from the current program and the previous two programs will
inform the Company's ongoing discussions with Peter Mac. Priority candidates from the initial
two programs have been shortlisted, and discussions are under way to advance their
development through a combination of in vitro assays and in vivo animal models.
In parallel with the Company's AI drug discovery activities, the commercial pharmaceutical
business continues to advance, with additional products and agreements progressing through
the pipeline. Algorae will continue to update shareholders as key commercial and scientific
milestones are achieved.
About Peter MacCallum Cancer Centre
Peter MacCallum Cancer Centre is a world-leading cancer research, education and
treatment centre and Australia’s only public health service solely dedicated to caring for
people affected by cancer. The Victorian Centre for Functional Genomics was established
over 16 years ago and is an internationally recognised technology platform (co-supported by
Phenomics Australia, a National Collaborative Research Infrastructure Strategy consortium)
that enables advanced high throughput screens using gene and drug targeting strategies
coupled with innovative image analytics.
Peter Mac currently treats more than 47,000 patients every year, combining care and
compassion with the latest research to deliver the best possible treatments, care and
outcomes for patients. This care is matched with world-class facilities within the Parkville
Biomedical Precinct and at six additional metropolitan and regional campuses.

About Algorae Pharmaceuticals
Algorae Pharmaceuticals (ASX: 1AI) is an AI-enabled pharmaceutical company with a dual focus on
drug-combination discovery and pharmaceutical commercialisation. The Company’s proprietary AI
platform, AlgoraeOS, applies machine learning and deep neural networks to identify synergistic drug
combinations and guide dose selection for preclinical development. In parallel, Algorae operates a
commercialisation business, AlgoraeRx, that sources, licenses and supplies generic and specialty
medicines in Australia and New Zealand through partnered manufacturers and established distribution
channels. Algorae collaborates with leading research institutions and industry partners to translate AI-
predicted therapies and to expand patient access to high-quality medicines.
Algorae is listed and publicly traded on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX: 1AI), providing investors
an opportunity to participate in the Company's growth.
For more information visit www.algoraepharma.com or follow @algoraepharma on X or LinkedIn.
